cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemRepair: Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Repository-Level Vulnerability Repair.
problema: Repository-level automated vulnerability repair treats each fix as an isolated one-shot generation, discarding prior fixes and failed validation attempts, so agents repeat cross-file security mistakes (e.g. integer overflow feeding an unguarded downstream write) that plain test feedback alone cannot correct.
mecanismo: A three-tier hierarchical memory (L1 History-Fix project-local fixes mined from CVEFixes, L2 Security-Pattern cross-project defensive patterns, L3 Refinement-Trajectory failure-to-success deltas) feeds a Locator-Patcher-Verifier loop; retrieval uses a two-priority intra-project-then-cross-project embedding search with dedup (cosine>=0.95) and recency-weighted pruning, and each verifier outcome (success/regenerate/relocate) writes new L2/L3 entries.
evaluacion: Evaluated on SEC-Bench (C/C++), PatchEval (Python/Go/JavaScript) and the C++ subset of Multi-SWE-bench, comparing against OpenHands, SWE-agent, Aider, Agentless and the specialized InfCode-C++, measuring % resolved, file-level location accuracy and average $/task repair cost.
numeros_clave: 58.0% resolved on SEC-Bench, 58.2% on PatchEval, 30.58%/30.6% on Multi-SWE-bench C++ vs InfCode-C++ 25.60% (+19% relative); >20pp over prior best general agents; L2=116/L3=86 stored entries reported for SEC-Bench; dedup threshold cosine>=0.95; refinement loop capped at 3 failed attempts (p.4-6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: L3 Refinement-Trajectory memory stores explicit failure-to-success deltas (P_fail, Delta_diff, insight) instead of discarding failed patches (§3.3.3, p.4) — a concrete pattern MF could adopt for negative-knowledge consolidation.
Deduplication (cosine>0.95 merge) plus recency-weighted pruning are lightweight rules that keep memory bounded and useful (§3.3.3), a reusable recipe for promoting/pruning MF's own gotcha store.
The paper measures retrieval quality explicitly via 'Location Accuracy' alongside success rate (§4.3, Table 2, p.6), matching MF's stance that retrieval must be measured, not assumed.
Cost ($/task) is a first-class reported metric and the refinement loop is explicitly capped at 3 attempts to bound cost (§4.4, p.6), supporting MF's context-economy stance.

notes: Table 2 (p.6, SEC-Bench/Multi-SWE-bench comparison) + §3.3.3 memory-scale figures (p.4) are the load-bearing evidence; clearly on-topic hierarchical + negative-knowledge memory paper, not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Feng et al. (2026). ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents.
problema: LLM agents solve each task from scratch, discarding successful strategies and failure lessons accumulated across prior interactions; fine-tuning the executor on this experience is brittle because it re-couples learning to one specific, soon-to-be-obsolete model.
mecanismo: Historical trajectories are distilled into skill (success) and lesson (failure) experience units stored as nodes of a self-evolving graph, with edges linking semantically/strategically related experiences; a lightweight RL-trained retrieval copilot predicts per-task diffusion depth (personalized PageRank) and a similarity-vs-utility ranking weight, retrieving beyond flat nearest-neighbor matching; node utility is updated online from with/without-retrieval task-score deltas while the executor LLM stays frozen.
evaluacion: Evaluated on ExpSuite (10 static QA/math/code benchmarks plus ALFWorld and AppWorld agentic environments) with Llama-3.2-3B/3.1-8B and Qwen3-32B/Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite executors, against retrieval-centric (Mem0, AWM, MemRL, ReasoningBank, ExpeL, LightMem) and LLM-centric (S3, IRCoT, Search-o1) baselines, with a component ablation.
numeros_clave: +12.2% (small executor) / +4.7% (large executor) average score over the strongest baseline on static tasks; +21.4%/+12.7% on agentic tasks; interaction-step reduction of 12.7%/21.6% vs the most efficient baseline (Abstract, §4.1, Table 2-3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Low-scoring trajectories are distilled into explicit 'lessons' (failure modes, invalid actions, constraints to avoid) stored as first-class graph nodes alongside skills (§3.2, p.4) — a concrete pattern for representing negative knowledge as retrievable structured memory rather than discarding failed attempts.

Retrieval utility is measured directly via a with/without-retrieval reward (Eq.14, p.5) and ablations isolate graph diffusion vs utility-ranking's separate contributions (§4) — matches MF's stance that retrieval quality must be measured.

Graph-structured relational memory with utility-aware ranking explicitly outperforms the flat nearest-neighbor retrieval used by Mem0/ExpeL/MemRL baselines (Table 1 p.2, Table 2 p.6) — a richer-index-over-flat-cache pattern MF could adopt for its derived index.

notes: Table 2/3 (pp.6-7) hold the load-bearing numbers; Table 1 (p.2) contrasts the capability matrix vs prior memory methods. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Raviotta (2026). Experience to Competence Without Weight Updates: Pre-Registered Falsifiable Gates for Agent Memory.
problema: Agent-memory evaluations are typically post-hoc (benchmarks and mechanisms chosen after the system already works) and negative results are rarely published, so it is unclear which biologically-inspired mechanisms (strengthening, decay, consolidation) actually help versus merely produce a plausible-looking in-system learning curve.
mecanismo: A SQLite-graph episodic/semantic memory with a same-fact LLM judge for dedup, reinforced/decaying edges, and nightly selective (verbatim, non-paraphrasing) consolidation is subjected to 5 pre-registered falsifiable gates (fixed pass/kill criteria, floor/ceiling arms, bootstrap CIs) run end-to-end locally via Ollama; a separate gate (M4) freezes the agent's weights and stores only verbatim API-error lessons, recalled by cosine top-k, to test experience-to-competence transfer with no gradient updates.
evaluacion: Five sequential gates (M0-M4) on synthetic fact-recall regimes and a 60-episode hidden-rule API task, each with a memoryless-control floor arm and an explicit-rules oracle ceiling arm, bootstrap 95% CIs (1000 resamples), replicated across 3 seeds for M4; all runs on a single consumer M1 Pro laptop.
numeros_clave: Repetition-weighted ranking KILLED vs vanilla cosine RAG: -0.440 [-0.527,-0.347] and -0.180 [-0.267,-0.100] (§6); cosine-similarity medians for same-fact paraphrases (0.83) fully overlap same-template distractors (0.87); consolidation compresses 350->150 active nodes at -0.053 statistical parity (§5-6); M4 first-try pass rate rises 0.45->1.00 across blocks vs control flat at 0.00 (oracle 0.95, Table 1 p.4), transfer effect replicates 3/3 seeds.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: M4 shows a frozen agent plus verbatim error-lesson memory converts API failures into transferable procedural competence (0.45->1.00) while a memoryless control stays at 0.00 across 60 episodes (§7, Table 1, p.4) — strong support for MF's investment in negative-knowledge (gotcha) memory.

Direct measurement shows cosine similarity CANNOT separate paraphrases of the same fact from same-template distractors (medians 0.83 vs 0.87, fully overlapping, §6, p.3) — embedding-only retrieval is structurally unsound, confirming MF's skepticism of embeddings as the primary index over grep/typed retrieval (ADR-019).

Selective consolidation with verbatim (non-paraphrase) merging compresses 350 exposures into 150 active nodes at statistical retention parity with store-everything (§5 M2, §6 ablation, p.3) — supports MF's promotion-not-summarization approach to durable memory.

'Verbatim beats gist, twice' (§8, p.5): LLM paraphrase corrupted exact values both in consolidation and lesson-writing, so the system stores verbatim text and reserves abstraction for retrieval time — echoes MF's docs-as-truth stance over lossy summarized indices.

notes: §6 Gate M3 (p.3) and §7 Gate M4 Table 1 (p.4) are the load-bearing measurements; two explicit KILLs of the celebrated repetition-ranking mechanism make this an unusually high-value negative-results paper. Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Wang and Li (2023). Learning from Mistakes via Cooperative Study Assistant for Large Language Models.
problema: LLM self-reflection methods rely on the model's own often-inaccurate judgment of when to stop refining, and are limited to the failed attempts of the current query, so agents cannot generalize error-avoidance guidance to similar future queries.
mecanismo: A cooperative auxiliary 'study assistant' agent compares the main LLM's responses against ground truth during a gathering phase, writing (query, wrong-answer, analysis+guideline) entries to a global mistake memory; at examination time (no ground truth available) it retrieves the top-k=1 most similar past mistake by cosine similarity (theta=0.9) and injects the analysis+guideline as pre-hoc instruction; the assistant can further be fine-tuned per-LLM via imitation learning on successful guidance trajectories.
evaluacion: Evaluated on 27 tasks from BBH (reasoning) and BBQ (social bias) across Flan-T5-11B, GPT-NeoX-20B and LLaMA-7B, against M (no memory), M w/Ocorr (correct-answer memory), M w/Oerr (mistake memory without feedback) and Self-Refine baselines, plus a 10%-training-data data-efficiency ablation.
numeros_clave: SALAM boosts accuracy up to +6.6 on BBH and +12.6 on BBQ over the best baseline (Abstract); Flan-T5 average BBH accuracy: M 42.4 -> SALAM 48.6 (Table 2, p.6); with only 10% training data SALAM still beats full-data M w/Ocorr and M w/Oerr on most BBH subtasks (Table 3, p.7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Directly measured: 'failure can sometimes be more valuable than success' — M w/Oerr (mistake memory) frequently outperforms M w/Ocorr (correct-answer memory) in Table 2 (p.6) — strong support for MF's investment in negative-knowledge (gotcha) memory over positive-example stores.

Retrieval is filtered by an explicit similarity threshold (theta=0.9, top-k=1) and its value is isolated against a no-feedback mistake-retrieval ablation (M w/Oerr) separating retrieval-only from retrieval+feedback gains (§4.3, p.6) — matches MF's measured-retrieval stance.

The study assistant is deliberately a small 7B model fine-tuned once and reused across all downstream tasks/LLMs rather than fine-tuning the large executor per task, explicitly framed as more cost-effective (§1 'Lightweight' advantage, p.2).

notes: Table 2 (p.6, main results) + the 'failure can sometimes be more valuable than success' discussion (p.6, §4.4). Clearly on-topic negative-knowledge memory paper; not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). StackPlanner: A Centralized Hierarchical Multi-Agent System with Task-Experience Memory Management.
problema: Centralized multi-agent coordinators accumulate task memory passively (fixed summarization/truncation), causing context bloat and error propagation over long-horizon tasks, and rarely reuse cross-task coordination experience, producing poor cold-start performance on novel tasks.
mecanismo: A hierarchical coordinator exposes memory operations as first-class RL-trained actions (PLAN/DELEGATE/REVISE/FINISH): REVISE actively condenses (pop-summarize-push) or prunes a LIFO task-memory stack, while a separate structured experience memory (user profiles, semantic facts, procedural SOPs) is retrieved cross-task to mitigate cold start; the whole policy (planning + memory + retrieval) is trained jointly with GRPO using a trajectory-level task-success reward plus a process reward tied to REVISE actions.
evaluacion: Evaluated on multi-hop QA (2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue), agentic benchmarks (GAIA, FRAMES) and open-ended DeepResearch Bench (RACE/FACT metrics) with Qwen2.5-3B/7B backbones, against Naive/Single-agent/Multi-agent/Agentic-RL baselines, plus a task-memory/experience-memory component ablation and a 100-instance multi-turn human-in-the-loop refinement test.
numeros_clave: Qwen2.5-3B F1 32.92/16.48/7.71/16.23 (2Wiki/MuSiQue/GAIA/FRAMES) rising to 38.34/22.01/9.45/19.44 with Qwen2.5-7B (Table 1, p.6); ablation on MuSiQue: removing task memory drops F1 16.48->10.76, removing experience memory ->8.99, removing both ->7.43 (Table 4, p.7); multi-turn refinement total score 71.11 vs 56-60 for ReAct baselines (Table 3, p.7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The coordinator's task-memory stack IS the plan/execution-trace state, explicitly separated from cross-task experience memory and manipulated only via a first-class REVISE action (push/condense/prune, §3.2, p.4) — direct precedent for treating plan-state itself as a governed memory tier, as MF's PLAN-ESTADO axis proposes.

REVISE's pruning path retains 'a concise record of failure causes... to guide subsequent exploration' when dropping unproductive memory segments (§3.1, p.4) — negative knowledge is preserved even when its raw trace is discarded, a pattern MF could adopt for gotcha compaction.

Active memory condensation/pruning is motivated explicitly as mitigating 'context bloat' and processing pressure on the central agent (§1 Challenge 1, p.1) and its value is measured via the ablation's accuracy delta (Table 4, p.7), supporting MF's context-economy stance that bounded, curated context beats unbounded accumulation.

notes: Table 1 (p.6, main benchmark) + Table 4 ablation (p.7) are load-bearing; plan_estado=SI is directly satisfied by the task-memory-stack design (§3.2, Fig.2, p.4). Not RECONSIDERAR.

cita: Sidik, B. y Rokach, L. (2026). MEMTIER: Tiered Memory Architecture and the Retrieval Bottleneck in Long-Running LLM Agents.
problema: Long-running agent runtimes (OpenClaw, 250k+ deployments) store all memory in flat MEMORY.md/daily-log files, causing four compounding failures (hard-cap truncation, compaction behavioural breaks, structural blindness of flat-text retrieval, and no attribution loop linking tool outcomes back to memory quality), degrading tool-success rates 14pp over a 72-hour window.
mecanismo: A tripartite plugin architecture: (1a) a structured episodic JSONL store with a cognitive-weight field updated from tool-outcome attribution; (1b) a 5-signal weighted BM25+decay+cognitive-weight+tier retrieval scorer with two-stage semantic-tier-then-episodic scoping; (1c) an attribution loop distributing tool-outcome credit to retrieved entries; (2a) an async consolidation daemon promoting episodic facts to a project-shared semantic tier via LLM extraction; (2b) a PPO trainer adapting the 5-signal weights from task-success reward.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the full LongMemEval-S (N=500, 5 ability types) with Qwen2.5-7B on a 6GB consumer GPU, plus LoCoMo for comparison, a full component-removal / retrieval-budget / token-budget ablation (Table 2), a BM25-normalisation probe, a dense-retrieval (bge-small) comparison, and an oracle-retrieval upper bound.
numeros_clave: Acc 0.050->0.382 (no-retrieval vs full system), F1 0.412; semantic pre-population is the dominant component (-0.128 Acc / ~2.9x F1 if removed); LLM-extracted facts ~3.1/question vs heuristic ~509/question (164x reduction, ~$0.05 total for 500 questions); oracle retrieval 0.550 vs system 0.350 (+0.200 gap); dense Stage-1 scoping +0.030 Acc overall but knowledge-update category regresses -0.125; PPO-learned weights numerically identical to defaults (Acc=0.382, Table 2/4, p.5-7).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The paper explicitly documents negative/null results — removing the cognitive-weight signal HELPS slightly (+0.012 to +0.014 Acc) and PPO weight-learning yields zero measurable gain (§4.4, Table 2/4, p.6-7) — a rare, honest admission of what does not work, confirming MF's need to capture negative findings as first-class knowledge.

The two-stage semantic-tier-to-episodic scoping acts as a derived cache narrowing the retrieval pool before full scoring (§3.2, removing it costs -0.040 Acc); the dense-vs-BM25 comparison shows a category-dependent tradeoff (multi-session +0.077, knowledge-update -0.125, §4.1, p.6-7) — a nuanced extension of MF's derived-index concept.

Token-efficiency finding: LLM-extracted facts (~3.1/question) beat heuristic extraction (~509/question) by ~2.9x F1 for ~$0.05 total preprocessing cost on 500 questions (§3, p.4) — precision beats coverage, directly confirming MF's context-economy stance.

Retrieval quality is measured directly (Recall@k, nDCG@4) and an oracle-retrieval upper bound (0.550 vs system 0.350, +0.200 gap) proves retrieval, not generation, is the bottleneck (§4.2, §5, p.7-8) — supports MF's insistence that retrieval must be measured.

notes: Table 2 ablation (p.5-6) + §4.1 dense-retrieval baseline + §4.4 PPO trainer (p.7) are the load-bearing measurements. Not RECONSIDERAR.
